fix(#851 r1, R3): Feature degrades by slicing the unconverted read, not by re-calling with waves=

On PeriodUnavailableError, Feature used to re-call the country with
waves=convertible.  food_quantities' default units='kgs' pools its kg
inference over the REQUESTED waves (GH #850), so the subset moved
non-period numbers: Mali 2014-15 +2.90% kg, Burkina Faso 2014 +0.73%,
Uganda 2019-20 44% of rows (red team r1).

Now: read the method WITHOUT period= (the frame an unconverted Feature
call gets), keep the convertible waves' rows and apply recall.to_period
to them (`_convert_convertible_waves`).  Kept rows are exactly the
unconverted rows times the per-t factor.  population / recall /
derivations attrs are re-attached for the slice by their own modules;
labels_unmatched still reports the whole read.

The warning no longer says "the countries' other waves were kept" for a
country dropped whole: it names the countries kept-restricted and the
countries dropped whole separately.

Branch-added fake-Country tests: the fixture monkeypatches
recall.recall_records (Feature now converts the slice itself), the
re-call pin `test_the_re_call_asks_for_exactly_the_convertible_waves`
is replaced by `test_the_second_read_is_the_unconverted_table_not_a_
wave_subset` (calls [(Beta, None, week), (Beta, None, None)]), and a
POOLED fake shows the old mechanism's error (Beta w7 per day: re-call
30.0, slice 60.0 = the unconverted 420 / 7).

+# The Recall Record and `period=`
+
+`food_expenditures` returns a number whose reference period used to be recorded
+nowhere. Most of the corpus is **7 days asked once**; GhanaLSS delivers **30
+days** (six five-day asks), Burkina Faso 2014 **28** of spending (four quarterly
+7-day passages) but **7** of quantity (only passage 1 fields the quantity grid),
+Mali 2014-15 **14** (two EACI passages of one panel, summed), Guatemala and
+Panama **15**. Pooling GhanaLSS with Ethiopia compared a 30-day figure with a
+7-day one, and nothing said so. GH #851.
+
+Two phases:
+
+1. **The record** (Phase I, 2026-09-09) — what window each `(country, wave)`
+   food cell covers, with its evidence rung. Facts only.
+2. **`period=`** (Phase II, ruling of @ligon 2026-10-18) — the one conversion
+   the record licenses, on `food_expenditures` and `food_quantities`.
+
+## The record
+
+```python
+import lsms_library as ll
+
+ll.recall()                         # every (country, wave), one row each
+ll.recall('GhanaLSS')
+df = ll.Country('Ethiopia').food_acquired()
+df.attrs['recall']                  # {country: {wave: RecallRecord}}
+```
+
+Each record carries four facts — kept separate because each is needed on its
+own:
+
+| field | meaning |
+|---|---|
+| `recall_days` | length of ONE ask |
+| `n_asks` | how many times the module is asked — **asks, not interviewer visits** (GLSS7 fields seven visits and asks food at six) |
+| `n_asks_by_column` | optional `{column: n}` for a flow column asked a different number of times than the module — Burkina Faso 2014 is `{Quantity: 1}` against `n_asks: 4`. It may name only `Expenditure` or `Quantity` and needs the evidence the count does |
+| `within_wave_variation` | the axis the window varies on *inside* the wave (`stratum`, `by-s`, …); when set, both numbers are null |
+| `basis` | the evidence rung: `questionnaire` > `variable-label` > `config-comment` > `filename` > `not-recorded` |
+
+`total_exposure_days = recall_days * n_asks` is a property, not a stored field;
+`rec.exposure_days(column)` is the same with the column's `n_asks_by_column`
+override, when it has one.
+The records live in `countries/{C}/_/recall.yml`, generated from the evidence
+base `.coder/coverage/food_recall.csv` by `scripts/promote_recall_records.py`;
+edit the CSV, not the YAML. The record rides through `Feature()` (GH #873).
+
+## `period=`
+
+```python
+eth = ll.Country('Ethiopia')
+eth.food_expenditures(period='day')            # each wave / its exposure
+eth.food_quantities(period='year', units='kgs')
+ll.Feature('food_expenditures')(period='month')
+```
+
+**Accepted values** — a closed vocabulary, one spelling each:
+
+| `period=` | days |
+|---|---|
+| `None` (default) | no conversion: the window the survey recorded |
+| `'day'` | 1 |
+| `'week'` | 7 |
+| `'month'` | 365.25 / 12 = 30.4375 |
+| `'year'` | 365.25 |
+
+`month` and `year` use the Julian year, the convention the only earlier in-repo
+conversion stated (`Togo/_/data_scheme.yml`). Anything else is a `ValueError`
+naming the list.
+
+**The conversion.** The derived tables sum `visit` away, so a row covers every
+ask of its column in the wave. Each row's flow column — `Expenditure` on
+`food_expenditures`, `Quantity` on `food_quantities` — is rescaled by its own
+wave's record:
+
+```
+value_in_period = value * period_days / (recall_days * n_asks_for(column))
+```
+
+where `n_asks_for(column)` is the column's `n_asks_by_column` entry if it has
+one, else `n_asks`. It is linear and per-`t`, so it commutes with the `labels=`
+re-aggregation, `market=` and `numeraire=`; `Country` applies it first. Nothing
+else in the frame changes — index, row count, other columns. The conversion is
+recorded on `df.attrs['period']`:
+
+```python
+out = ll.Country('GhanaLSS').food_expenditures(waves=['2016-17'], period='year')
+out.attrs['period']['GhanaLSS']
+# {'period': 'year', 'period_days': 365.25, 'columns': ['Expenditure'],
+#  'waves': {'2016-17': {'exposure_days': 30.0, 'factor': 12.175,
+#            'recall_days': 5.0, 'n_asks': 6, 'n_asks_source': 'n_asks',
+#            'basis': 'questionnaire', 'ask_count_basis': 'measured'}}}
+```
+
+`n_asks_source` is `'n_asks_by_column'` where the column's own count was used
+(Burkina Faso 2014's `food_quantities`).
+
+**Read `basis` before trusting a converted number.** `config-comment` means a
+maintainer asserted the window in repo prose; it converts (the ruling counted
+those cells), but it is not a questionnaire.
+
+### Which tables accept it
+
+| table | `period=` |
+|---|---|
+| `food_expenditures`, `food_quantities` | accepted |
+| `food_prices` | **refused** — `TypeError`. A price is a rate per unit of the good, not a flow over time; rescaling it by a recall window changes its meaning, not its period. |
+| `food_acquired` | refused — it keeps the `visit` level, so a row covers ONE ask, not the cell's exposure |
+| every other table | refused — `TypeError`, as for any kwarg a table does not take |
+
+A refusal happens before any data is read, from `Country(...)` and from
+`Feature(...)` alike (the two share one message, `recall.period_refusal`).
+
+### Where the window is unknown: Contract B
+
+The third instance of the pattern `labels=` (`LabelUnavailableError`) and
+`units=` (`UnitsUnavailableError`) already follow.
+
+**`Country(...)` raises** `lsms_library.errors.PeriodUnavailableError` (a
+`ValueError`) when the result holds ANY wave whose window is not established,
+and converts nothing:
+
+```python
+from lsms_library.errors import PeriodUnavailableError
+try:
+    ll.Country('Nigeria').food_expenditures(period='week')
+except PeriodUnavailableError as e:
+    e.unavailable   # {'2018Q3': "the window varies within the wave (within_wave_variation='by-s') ...", '2019Q1': ...}
+    e.convertible   # ['2010Q3', '2011Q1', '2012Q3', '2013Q1', '2015Q3', '2016Q1']
+    ll.Country('Nigeria').food_expenditures(period='week', waves=e.convertible)
+```
+
+A wave is refused when its record is absent, varies within the wave, rests on
+a weak rung (`not-recorded`, `filename`), or lacks `recall_days` / `n_asks`.
+It raises rather than returning the known waves converted and the rest
+unscaled (one column on two clocks) or filling them with `NA` (which `sum()`
+reads as zero — GH #828).
+
+**`Feature(...)` degrades — at the grain of the WAVE.** A country whose other
+waves convert is **kept, restricted to them**; a country with none is dropped.
+One aggregated warning names every dropped `(country, wave)` cell, and the
+assembled frame carries them:
+
+```python
+df = ll.Feature('food_expenditures')(period='year')
+df.attrs['period_unavailable']   # {'GhanaLSS': ['1991-92'], 'Malawi': [...], ...}
+df.attrs['period']               # one conversion record per kept country
+```
+
+This is a deliberate departure from the `labels=` / `units=` precedent, which
+drops whole countries. The window is a property of the `(country, wave)` cell,
+not of the country: dropping by country would discard GhanaLSS's six
+convertible waves for its one stratified wave — exactly the cells `period=`
+exists to compare — and would keep 17 of the 32 convertible cells instead of
+32.
+
+**How a degraded country is converted: a slice of the unconverted read.**
+`Feature` reads the country's table again *without* `period=` — the very frame
+an unconverted `Feature` call gets — keeps the rows of the convertible waves,
+and applies the same conversion to them. So for every kept row:
+
+```
+Feature(t)(period=p, **kw) row  ==  Feature(t)(**kw) row  x  its wave's factor
+```
+
+exactly — bit-for-bit, measured on Mali and Burkina Faso (`food_quantities`,
+default `units='kgs'`), Uganda (`units='kgs'`, `labels='Aggregate'`,
+`market='Region'`), GhanaLSS and Nigeria (`food_expenditures` with
+`labels='Aggregate'`, `market='Region'`; `food_quantities` with `units='kgs'`,
+`labels='Aggregate'`), and pinned by `TestDeliveredFeature`. The second read
+costs time: 146 s against 104 s for the unconverted
+`Feature('food_expenditures')()` on the full corpus.
+
+*Why not re-call the country with `waves=` its convertible waves* (the first
+version): `food_quantities(units='kgs')` infers kg factors by pooling over the
+waves *requested* (GH #850), so a wave subset moved numbers that have nothing to
+do with `period=` — Mali 2014-15 +2.90% kg (49,312 of 108,711 rows changed),
+Burkina Faso 2014 +0.73%, Uganda 2019-20 44% of rows (red team r1, R3). A slice
+of the unconverted read moves none. The per-wave `attrs` records (`population`,
+`recall`, `derivations`) are re-attached for the slice, so they describe the
+rows served; `labels_unmatched` still reports the whole read.
+
+`Country(c).<table>(waves=e.convertible, period=p)` — the escape hatch the
+error names — remains a *subset request*: under `units='kgs'` its rows can
+differ from the `Feature` rows for the same waves, for the GH #850 reason
+above.

+

+  exposure, one constant per wave. Dividing by the *realised* interval is
+  refuted on this corpus — on GLSS4, doubling the gap between visits moves
+  reported spend +1.2% where proportionality predicts +100% — so it would
+  inject fieldwork tempo rather than normalise (`lsms_library/recall.py`
+  module docstring; Scott and Amenuvegbe 1990).

+  survey is entirely first-ask; GhanaLSS's 30 days spread one first-ask premium

+# (``.coder/charter-recall-windows.md``) records why the ask-order bias does

+# total estimates consumption is a measurement question ``food_expenditures``
+# already carries.  What the conversion does NOT do is equalise that bias --
+# a single-ask 7-day survey is entirely first-ask, GhanaLSS's 30 days spread

+# Said in ``docs/guide/recall.md`` beside the kwarg; not a reason to withhold.
+
+#: ``df.attrs`` key holding ``{country: {...conversion record...}}``.
+PERIOD_ATTRS_KEY = "period"

+#: Accepted ``period=`` values and their length in days.  Closed: one
+#: spelling per period.  ``month`` and ``year`` use the Julian year
+#: (365.25 days), the convention the only prior in-repo conversion stated
+#: (``Togo/_/data_scheme.yml``, ``Expenditure * 365.25 / days``).
+PERIOD_DAYS: dict[str, float] = {
+    "day": 1.0,
+    "week": 7.0,
+    "month": 365.25 / 12,
+    "year": 365.25,
+}
+
+#: The tables ``period=`` is defined on, and the FLOW columns it scales.
+#: Deliberately excludes ``food_prices`` (a price is a rate per unit, not a
+#: flow over time; see :func:`period_refusal`) and ``food_acquired`` (its
+#: ``visit`` level is not summed, so a row covers ONE ask, not the cell's
+#: exposure -- a different denominator, and not in Phase II's scope).
+PERIOD_TABLES: dict[str, tuple[str, ...]] = {
+    "food_expenditures": ("Expenditure",),
+    "food_quantities": ("Quantity",),
+}
+
+#: Every column :data:`PERIOD_TABLES` scales -- the names
+#: ``RecallRecord.n_asks_by_column`` may override.  One flow column per
+#: table, so a table's ``attrs['period']`` describes exactly one column.
+FLOW_COLUMNS: tuple[str, ...] = tuple(sorted(
+    {c for cols in PERIOD_TABLES.values() for c in cols}))
+
+
+def period_days(period: str) -> float:
+    """Length of *period* in days; ``ValueError`` on anything else."""
+    try:
+        return PERIOD_DAYS[period]
+    except (KeyError, TypeError):
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"period= must be one of {list(PERIOD_DAYS)} (or None for the "
+            f"window the survey recorded); got {period!r}") from None
+
+
+def period_refusal(table: str) -> str:
+    """The ``TypeError`` message for ``period=`` on a table that refuses it.
+
+    One message for ``Country`` and ``Feature`` so the two cannot drift.
+    ``food_prices`` gets its own sentence, because it is the table someone
+    will add ``period=`` to "for symmetry" unless the refusal says why.
+    """
+    head = (f"{table}() got an unexpected keyword argument 'period'; only "
+            f"{sorted(PERIOD_TABLES)} accept it.")
+    if table == "food_prices":
+        return (head + "  A price is a rate per unit of the good, not a "
+                "flow over time: it has no reference period to convert, and "
+                "rescaling it by a recall window would change its meaning, "
+                "not its period (GH #851).")
+    if table == "food_acquired":
+        return (head + "  food_acquired keeps the `visit` level, so a row "
+                "covers ONE ask rather than the cell's total exposure; derive "
+                "food_expenditures / food_quantities, which sum it away.")
+    return head
+

+def unavailable_reason(rec: RecallRecord | None) -> str | None:
+    """Why *rec* does not establish a window ``period=`` may divide by.
+
+    ``None`` means it does: ``total_exposure_days`` is known and rests on a
+    rung stronger than a guess.  The order is the order a reader needs:
+
+    1. no record at all -- the wave was never entered in ``recall.yml``;
+    2. ``within_wave_variation`` -- there is no single window to divide by
+       (GhanaLSS 1991-92 by stratum, Nigeria 2018Q3/2019Q1 by source), so
+       no per-wave factor is correct for every row;
+    3. a WEAK rung (``not-recorded``, ``filename``) -- ``not-recorded``
+       carries no number by construction, and a ``filename`` window is a
+       guess the record itself tells consumers to discount;
+    4. a recorded rung whose ``recall_days`` or ``n_asks`` is blank.

+    rung rides on ``attrs['period']`` so a consumer can discount them.
+    """

+        return "no recall record for this wave"

+                f"no single factor is right for every row")

+    return None

+def to_period(df, country: str, period: str, *, table: str,

+
+    Each row's flow column (``Expenditure`` / ``Quantity``, per
+    :data:`PERIOD_TABLES`) is multiplied by ``PERIOD_DAYS[period] /
+    exposure_days(column)`` of its own wave ``t`` -- ``recall_days *
+    n_asks``, or the column's ``n_asks_by_column`` override.  Linear and
+    per-``t``, so it commutes with the ``labels=`` re-aggregation,
+    ``market=`` and ``numeraire=`` post-steps: ``Country`` applies it before

+    the unconverted frame, and the two agree.

+    (:func:`unavailable_reason`), nothing is converted and
+    :class:`~lsms_library.errors.PeriodUnavailableError` is raised naming
+    every such wave and the convertible ones.  Converting the known waves and
+    leaving the rest unscaled would return one column on two clocks; filling
+    the unknown ones with NA would read as zero under ``sum()`` (GH #828).
+    ``Feature`` degrades over the error at the wave grain: it reads the
+    table without ``period=``, keeps the rows of ``.convertible`` waves and
+    converts those with this function.

+    Returns a COPY carrying ``attrs[PERIOD_ATTRS_KEY] = {country: {...}}``:
+    the target, its length in days, the scaled column and, per wave, the
+    column's exposure, factor, ``recall_days``, ``n_asks``, where that count
+    came from (``n_asks_source``: ``'n_asks'`` or ``'n_asks_by_column'``) and
+    both rungs -- so a ``config-comment`` window is visibly weaker than a
+    ``questionnaire`` one on the frame itself.  Plain dicts and numbers only
+    (``df.to_parquet`` serialises ``attrs`` with a bare ``json.dumps``).
+
+    *records* defaults to :func:`recall_records` for *country*; tests pass
+    their own.
+    """
+    import pandas as pd
+
+    from .errors import PeriodUnavailableError
+
+    target = period_days(period)
+    if table not in PERIOD_TABLES:
+        raise TypeError(period_refusal(table))
+    cols = [c for c in PERIOD_TABLES[table] if c in df.columns]
+    if not cols:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{country}: {table}(period={period!r}) found none of the flow "
+            f"columns {list(PERIOD_TABLES[table])} to rescale; got "
+            f"{list(df.columns)}")
+    names = list(df.index.names or [])
+    if "t" not in names:
+        raise ValueError(
+            f"{country}: {table}(period={period!r}) needs a `t` index level "
+            f"to look each row's window up by wave; got {names}")

+        records = recall_records(country)
+

+    # and a categorical or nullable-string level must look up the same way.
+    t_str = (df.index.get_level_values("t").astype("string")
+             .to_numpy(dtype=object, na_value=pd.NA))
+    # One flow column per table (FLOW_COLUMNS), so ``col`` is the column the
+    # factor -- and the attrs record -- describe.  Its exposure is the
+    # record's, unless ``n_asks_by_column`` names it (Burkina Faso 2014's
+    # Quantity: one ask of four).
+    col = cols[0]
+    factors: dict[str, float] = {}
+    unavailable: dict[str, str] = {}
+    for w in pd.unique(t_str):
+        if w is None or w is pd.NA:
+            unavailable["<NA>"] = "the row's wave `t` is missing (NaN key)"
+            continue
+        rec = records.get(str(w))
+        why = unavailable_reason(rec)
+        if why is not None:
+            unavailable[str(w)] = why
+        else:
+            factors[str(w)] = target / rec.exposure_days(col)
+    if unavailable:
+        raise PeriodUnavailableError(
+            country=country, period=period, table=table,
+            unavailable=unavailable, convertible=factors)
+
+    out = df.copy()
+    factor = pd.Series(t_str).map(factors).to_numpy(dtype=float)
+    out[col] = out[col] * factor
+    out.attrs = dict(df.attrs)
+
+    def _wave(rec: RecallRecord) -> dict[str, Any]:
+        overridden = col in (rec.n_asks_by_column or {})
+        return {
+            "exposure_days": float(rec.exposure_days(col)),
+            "factor": target / rec.exposure_days(col),
+            "recall_days": float(rec.recall_days),
+            "n_asks": int(rec.n_asks_for(col)),
+            "n_asks_source": "n_asks_by_column" if overridden else "n_asks",
+            "basis": rec.basis,
+            "ask_count_basis": rec.ask_count_basis,
+        }
+
+    record = {
+        "period": period,
+        "period_days": target,
+        "columns": cols,
+        "waves": {w: _wave(records[w]) for w in sorted(factors)},
+    }
+    existing = out.attrs.get(PERIOD_ATTRS_KEY)
+    merged = dict(existing) if isinstance(existing, dict) else {}
+    merged[country] = record
+    out.attrs[PERIOD_ATTRS_KEY] = merged
+    return out
+
+
+def merge_period_attrs(frames) -> dict[str, dict[str, Any]]:
+    """Union the ``period`` attrs of several frames, for ``Feature()`` assembly.
+
+    The twin of :func:`merge_attrs`, for the same reason: the cross-country
+    ``concat`` disagrees by design (one record per country) and lands in the
+    ``{}`` case, so ``feature._ATTRS_CARRIERS`` re-attaches this.  Elements
+    may be frames or captured ``attrs`` mappings.
+    """
+    out: dict[str, dict[str, Any]] = {}
+    for f in frames:
+        got = (getattr(f, "attrs", f) or {}).get(PERIOD_ATTRS_KEY)
+        if isinstance(got, dict):
+            out.update(got)
+    return out

+"""GH #851 Phase II: ``period=`` on ``food_expenditures`` / ``food_quantities``.
+
+Ruling (@ligon, 2026-10-18): ship ``period=`` under Contract B -- a typed raise
+from ``Country()``, a degrade plus warning from ``Feature()`` -- and refuse it
+on ``food_prices``.  Design and coverage: ``docs/guide/recall.md``.
+
+One test (at least) per branch:
+
+* the vocabulary (``PERIOD_DAYS``) and its refusals;
+* :func:`recall.unavailable_reason` -- one reason per way a window can fail
+  to be established, and ``config-comment`` DOES convert;
+* :func:`recall.to_period` -- the arithmetic, the strict raise, the
+  ``attrs['period']`` record (JSON-serialisable), commutation with a re-sum;
+* the generated ``Country`` method -- conversion, the typed raise naming the
+  country, ``waves=`` as the escape hatch, refusal on ``food_prices`` /
+  ``food_acquired`` / a non-food table, no legacy fall-through under
+  ``period=``, and ``period=None`` unchanged (``_aggregate_wave_data``
+  monkeypatched; no data read);
+* ``Feature`` -- refusal up front, the wave-grain degrade with ONE warning and
+  ``attrs['period_unavailable']``, and the ``period`` carrier surviving the
+  concat (fake ``Country``; no data read);
+* coverage -- every recorded cell is classified, and the count the guide
+  states is the count the records give;
+* ``TestDelivered`` -- the same on real built tables; skipped when cold.
+"""
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+import json
+import re
+import sys
+import warnings
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import numpy as np
+import pandas as pd
+import pytest
+
+import lsms_library.feature  # noqa: F401  (bind the submodule, not ll.recall)
+import lsms_library.recall  # noqa: F401
+from lsms_library.errors import PeriodUnavailableError
+
+F = sys.modules["lsms_library.feature"]
+R = sys.modules["lsms_library.recall"]
+
+REPO = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent
+
+
+def rec(wave, **kw):
+    return R.RecallRecord(country="Someland", wave=wave, **kw)
